quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Several factors affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Which one does NOT affect it?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast a person drinks
Body weight
Height

questions.correctAnswerText: Height
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: A driver is merging from an entrance ramp into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Move to the next lane if you can.
Do not worry about it. They should avoid you.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the next lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Give merging drivers plenty of space by moving to another lane if possible. They may not see your motorcycle.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?

options.text: After starting the motorcycle
Before starting the motorcycle
While riding
At a traffic signal

questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting the motorcycle
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before you start your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and the lane beside you.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's total braking power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Severe
Left to the judge's decision
Not very serious
Optional

questions.correctAnswerText: Severe
questions.explanation: Oregon law has severe mandatory penalties for drinking and riding. Riding under the influence is both illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Why should you use both front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop?

options.text: Using one brake alone causes uneven wear
It builds good braking habits for emergencies
It is the only way to slow a motorcycle
The brakes only work when both are used

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops creates a habit. This habit will help you in emergencies when using both brakes may be critical.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Often
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. You will usually notice tire failure by how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: You are passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic. Where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane
Stay toward the left side of your lane
Look to your left frequently
Use your rearview mirrors more often

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane
questions.explanation: Stay on the side of your lane away from the parked cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out between cars.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo, what happens to your motorcycle's speed?

options.text: It accelerates faster but stops slower
It accelerates slower and stops slower
It accelerates slower but stops faster
It accelerates faster and stops faster

questions.correctAnswerText: It accelerates slower and stops slower
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle take longer to speed up and longer to stop.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one brake in non-emergency situations.
Use both brakes only on wet pavement.
Use both brakes in all situations.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes in all situations.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the tire that is still good.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and slow down gradually. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is still good. Move toward the side of the road as you slow down, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective riding gear?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that cover your ankles
Hearing protection
Pants made of soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or strong material, boots that cover and support your ankles, and hearing protection even with a helmet.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and never use it again.
Release the front brake, then squeeze it hard right away.
Release the front brake immediately, then apply it smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then apply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply the brake smoothly again.

questions.question: Before riding, you should check everything except:

options.text: Your tire pressure.
How much tread is left on your tires.
How reflective your tires are.
The general condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.correctAnswerText: How reflective your tires are.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tire tread, and the condition of the sidewalls and tread surface.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is securely fastened.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is securely fastened is the single best thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle for a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handlebar in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handlebar in the opposite direction of the turn.
Apply the front brake.
Apply the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handlebar in the direction you want to turn to make this happen.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is true?

options.text: You can complete a pass in a no passing zone.
You can go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
You must start and complete the pass in a passing zone.
You must complete the pass on the shoulder if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and complete the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: A pass must be completed within the posted speed limit and only where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: If you find yourself riding beside another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up or slow down.
Wave at the other driver.
Stay beside the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the other driver handle it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding directly beside another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears. Speed up or drop back to get away from the other vehicle.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?

options.text: On the left handlebar
On the right handlebar
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handlebar
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is usually on the right handlebar. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Slow down with your brakes before shifting to a lower gear.
Speed up before shifting to a lower gear.
Swerve to the left.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you that you are downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down with your brakes before shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: You must slow down enough before shifting to a lower gear. Downshifting at high speed can cause the motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel to slip. Use your brakes to reach a safe speed before downshifting.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Signal your turns and use your brake light to show your intentions.
Look for hazards in your path.
Hope other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, signal your actions, and stay aware of hazards. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you. Instead, take active steps to protect yourself.

questions.question: Riding alongside another rider:

options.text: Lets you use more of the road.
Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
Lets you talk to the other rider.
Makes it easier for other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcyclist. This limits both riders' escape routes if danger appears.

questions.question: Goggles can:

options.text: Protect your eyes and your face.
Protect your face but not your eyes.
Protect your eyes, but not your face.
Not protect your face or eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield can protect your whole face.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance:

options.text: If the road is slippery.
If there are only a few vehicles on the road.
If the sun is shining.
If drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your distance behind other vehicles when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Slippery pavement, poor visibility, or heavy traffic all require more following distance.
